planting.note: Plant corms in fall (September-November in zone 9) for winter and spring bloom; pre-soak corms 3-4 hours in cool water before planting to rehydrate. Plant with the claw-like corm facing downward, 2 inches deep.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately moist soil — ranunculus requires excellent drainage, especially in winter, since wet soil causes corm rot. Tecolote Rose is a named color selection in the Tecolote Series, one of the finest commercial ranunculus strains available, producing large, fully double, multi-petaled flowers in a clear rose-pink that resemble a perfectly formed, layered rose or peony at three to four inches across. The tissue-thin petals packed in dense concentric rings hold up beautifully as a cut flower, lasting one to two weeks in a vase. In zone 9, planted in fall for February-April bloom, it provides a spectacular spring floral display during the late-winter window when few other garden plants flower at this level of quality. The corms cannot tolerate summer heat; dig and store in a cool, dry location after foliage yellows, or treat as an annual and replace each fall.
sources: University of California Cooperative Extension — Ranunculus asiaticus Tecolote Series Production

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately moist soil — ranunculus requires excellent drainage, especially in winter, since wet soil causes corm rot. Its scaled-down size still delivers the same richly layered, rose-like double flower form in a range of bright colors. In zone 9, planted in fall for February-April bloom, it provides a spectacular spring floral display during the late-winter window when few other garden plants flower at this level of quality.
